title: Fix Lua DNS dissector example edge cases
description:
Two problems are fixed in the DNS dissector Lua example:
- Queries for the root zone (`.`) use an empty name field with only the null terminator. The query parser would fail, and the minimum question length was too low.
- When parsing a query containing multiple questions, all question trees would display the query type and class from the first question.

Multi-question queries [aren't in real world use](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4082081/requesting-a-and-aaaa-records-in-single-dns-query/4083071#4083071), but this example is used by people (like me) writing other dissectors with similar patterns.

To demonstrate these problems, set up the example dissector, start a wireshark capture for `port 53 and host 8.8.8.8`, and run the following in the `scapy` CLI:
```python
sr1(IP(dst="8.8.8.8")/UDP(dport=53)/
    DNS(id=0,rd=1,qd=DNSQR(qname=".",qtype="NS")))
sr1(IP(dst="8.8.8.8")/UDP(dport=53)/
    DNS(id=1,rd=1,qd=
        DNSQR(qname="example.com",qtype="NS")/
        DNSQR(qname="example.com",qtype="A")/
        DNSQR(qname="example.com",qtype="AAAA")))
```

If you want regression tests I'll figure out how to do that.

Aside: It's silly that the C DNS dissector says the length of the root zone name is 6, but I can't imagine a realistic situation where that would be more than an oddity.

commits_data.title: Lua: DNS: Fix Fields for multi-question queries
commits_data.message:
Lua: DNS: Fix Fields for multi-question queries

`my_field().display` uses the first FieldInfo in the multival, so all
question trees would display the type and class from the first question.

Queries with more than one question aren't used on the modern internet,
but let's handle it correctly anyway in the example code.

commits_data.title: Lua: Fix root zone queries in DNS example
commits_data.message:
Lua: Fix root zone queries in DNS example

Queries for the root zone (e.g. `dig -t NS`) produce a name of only `\x00`,
which would cause the query parser to fail.
